NKJV.1: “Now take Aaron your brother, and his sons with him, from among the children of Israel, that he may minister to Me as priest, Aaron and Aaron’s sons: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
NKJV.2: And you shall make holy garments for Aaron your brother, for glory and for beauty.
NKJV.3: So you shall speak to all who are gifted artisans, whom I have filled with the spirit of wisdom, that they may make Aaron’s garments, to consecrate him, that he may minister to Me as priest.
NKJV.4: And these are the garments which they shall make: a breastplate, an ephod, a robe, a skillfully woven tunic, a turban, and a sash. So they shall make holy garments for Aaron your brother and his sons, that he may minister to Me as priest.
NKJV.5: “They shall take the gold, blue, purple, and scarlet thread, and the fine linen,
NKJV.6: and they shall make the ephod of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet thread, and fine woven linen, artistically worked.
NKJV.7: It shall have two shoulder straps joined at its two edges, and so it shall be joined together.
NKJV.8: And the intricately woven band of the ephod, which is on it, shall be of the same workmanship, made of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet thread, and fine woven linen.
NKJV.9: “Then you shall take two onyx stones and engrave on them the names of the sons of Israel:
NKJV.10: six of their names on one stone and six names on the other stone, in order of their birth.
NKJV.11: With the work of an engraver in stone, like the engravings of a signet, you shall engrave the two stones with the names of the sons of Israel. You shall set them in settings of gold.
NKJV.12: And you shall put the two stones on the shoulders of the ephod as memorial stones for the sons of Israel. So Aaron shall bear their names before the LORD on his two shoulders as a memorial.
NKJV.13: You shall also make settings of gold,
NKJV.14: and you shall make two chains of pure gold like braided cords, and fasten the braided chains to the settings.
NKJV.15: “You shall make the breastplate of judgment. Artistically woven according to the workmanship of the ephod you shall make it: of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet thread, and fine woven linen, you shall make it.
NKJV.16: It shall be doubled into a square: a span shall be its length, and a span shall be its width.
NKJV.17: And you shall put settings of stones in it, four rows of stones: The first row shall be a sardius, a topaz, and an emerald; this shall be the first row;
NKJV.18: the second row shall be a turquoise, a sapphire, and a diamond;
NKJV.19: the third row, a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst;
NKJV.20: and the fourth row, a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper. They shall be set in gold settings.
NKJV.21: And the stones shall have the names of the sons of Israel, twelve according to their names, like the engravings of a signet, each one with its own name; they shall be according to the twelve tribes.
NKJV.22: “You shall make chains for the breastplate at the end, like braided cords of pure gold.
NKJV.23: And you shall make two rings of gold for the breastplate, and put the two rings on the two ends of the breastplate.
NKJV.24: Then you shall put the two braided chains of gold in the two rings which are on the ends of the breastplate;
NKJV.25: and the other two ends of the two braided chains you shall fasten to the two settings, and put them on the shoulder straps of the ephod in the front.
NKJV.26: “You shall make two rings of gold, and put them on the two ends of the breastplate, on the edge of it, which is on the inner side of the ephod.
NKJV.27: And two other rings of gold you shall make, and put them on the two shoulder straps, underneath the ephod toward its front, right at the seam above the intricately woven band of the ephod.
NKJV.28: They shall bind the breastplate by means of its rings to the rings of the ephod, using a blue cord, so that it is above the intricately woven band of the ephod, and so that the breastplate does not come loose from the ephod.
NKJV.29: “So Aaron shall bear the names of the sons of Israel on the breastplate of judgment over his heart, when he goes into the holy place, as a memorial before the LORD continually.
NKJV.30: And you shall put in the breastplate of judgment the Urim and the Thummim, and they shall be over Aaron’s heart when he goes in before the LORD. So Aaron shall bear the judgment of the children of Israel over his heart before the LORD continually.
NKJV.31: “You shall make the robe of the ephod all of blue.
NKJV.32: There shall be an opening for his head in the middle of it; it shall have a woven binding all around its opening, like the opening in a coat of mail, so that it does not tear.
NKJV.33: And upon its hem you shall make pomegranates of blue, purple, and scarlet, all around its hem, and bells of gold between them all around:
NKJV.34: a golden bell and a pomegranate, a golden bell and a pomegranate, upon the hem of the robe all around.
NKJV.35: And it shall be upon Aaron when he ministers, and its sound will be heard when he goes into the holy place before the LORD and when he comes out, that he may not die.
NKJV.36: “You shall also make a plate of pure gold and engrave on it, like the engraving of a signet: HOLINESS TO THE LORD.
NKJV.37: And you shall put it on a blue cord, that it may be on the turban; it shall be on the front of the turban.
NKJV.38: So it shall be on Aaron’s forehead, that Aaron may bear the iniquity of the holy things which the children of Israel hallow in all their holy gifts; and it shall always be on his forehead, that they may be accepted before the LORD.
NKJV.39: “You shall skillfully weave the tunic of fine linen thread, you shall make the turban of fine linen, and you shall make the sash of woven work.
NKJV.40: “For Aaron’s sons you shall make tunics, and you shall make sashes for them. And you shall make hats for them, for glory and beauty.
NKJV.41: So you shall put them on Aaron your brother and on his sons with him. You shall anoint them, consecrate them, and sanctify them, that they may minister to Me as priests.
NKJV.42: And you shall make for them linen trousers to cover their nakedness; they shall reach from the waist to the thighs.
NKJV.43: They shall be on Aaron and on his sons when they come into the tabernacle of meeting, or when they come near the altar to minister in the holy place, that they do not incur iniquity and die. It shall be a statute forever to him and his descendants after him.

NASB.1: 'Then bring near to yourself Aaron your brother, and his sons with him, from among the sons of Israel, to minister as priest to Me-- Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron's sons.
NASB.2: 'You shall make holy garments for Aaron your brother, for glory and for beauty.
NASB.3: 'You shall speak to all the skillful persons whom I have endowed with the spirit of wisdom, that they make Aaron's garments to consecrate him, that he may minister as priest to Me.
NASB.4: 'These are the garments which they shall make: a breastpiece and an ephod and a robe and a tunic of checkered work, a turban and a sash, and they shall make holy garments for Aaron your brother and his sons, that he may minister as priest to Me.
NASB.5: 'They shall take the gold and the blue and the purple and the scarlet [material] and the fine linen.
NASB.6: 'They shall also make the ephod of gold, of blue and purple [and] scarlet [material] and fine twisted linen, the work of the skillful workman.
NASB.7: 'It shall have two shoulder pieces joined to its two ends, that it may be joined.
NASB.8: 'The skillfully woven band, which is on it, shall be like its workmanship, of the same material: of gold, of blue and purple and scarlet [material] and fine twisted linen.
NASB.9: 'You shall take two onyx stones and engrave on them the names of the sons of Israel,
NASB.10: six of their names on the one stone and the names of the remaining six on the other stone, according to their birth.
NASB.11: 'As a jeweler engraves a signet, you shall engrave the two stones according to the names of the sons of Israel; you shall set them in filigree [settings] of gold.
NASB.12: 'You shall put the two stones on the shoulder pieces of the ephod, [as] stones of memorial for the sons of Israel, and Aaron shall bear their names before the LORD on his two shoulders for a memorial.
NASB.14: and two chains of pure gold; you shall make them of twisted cordage work, and you shall put the corded chains on the filigree [settings].
NASB.15: 'You shall make a breastpiece of judgment, the work of a skillful workman; like the work of the ephod you shall make it: of gold, of blue and purple and scarlet [material] and fine twisted linen you shall make it.
NASB.16: 'It shall be square [and] folded double, a span in length and a span in width.
NASB.17: 'You shall mount on it four rows of stones; the first row [shall be] a row of ruby, topaz and emerald;
NASB.18: and the second row a turquoise, a sapphire and a diamond;
NASB.19: and the third row a jacinth, an agate and an amethyst;
NASB.20: and the fourth row a beryl and an onyx and a jasper; they shall be set in gold filigree.

NLT.1: “Call for your brother, Aaron, and his sons, Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. Set them apart from the rest of the people of Israel so they may minister to me and be my priests.
NLT.2: Make sacred garments for Aaron that are glorious and beautiful.

NLT.4: These are the garments they are to make: a chestpiece, an ephod, a robe, a patterned tunic, a turban, and a sash. They are to make these sacred garments for your brother, Aaron, and his sons to wear when they serve me as priests.

NLT.6: “The craftsmen must make the ephod of finely woven linen and skillfully embroider it with gold and with blue, purple, and scarlet thread.
NLT.7: It will consist of two pieces, front and back, joined at the shoulders with two shoulder-pieces.
NLT.8: The decorative sash will be made of the same materials: finely woven linen embroidered with gold and with blue, purple, and scarlet thread.
NLT.9: “Take two onyx stones, and engrave on them the names of the tribes of Israel.
NLT.10: Six names will be on each stone, arranged in the order of the births of the original sons of Israel.
NLT.11: Engrave these names on the two stones in the same way a jeweler engraves a seal. Then mount the stones in settings of gold filigree.
NLT.12: Fasten the two stones on the shoulder-pieces of the ephod as a reminder that Aaron represents the people of Israel. Aaron will carry these names on his shoulders as a constant reminder whenever he goes before the LORD.
NLT.13: Make the settings of gold filigree,
NLT.14: then braid two cords of pure gold and attach them to the filigree settings on the shoulders of the ephod.
NLT.15: “Then, with great skill and care, make a chestpiece to be worn for seeking a decision from God. Make it to match the ephod, using finely woven linen embroidered with gold and with blue, purple, and scarlet thread.
NLT.16: Make the chestpiece of a single piece of cloth folded to form a pouch nine inches square.
NLT.17: Mount four rows of gemstones on it. The first row will contain a red carnelian, a pale-green peridot, and an emerald.
NLT.18: The second row will contain a turquoise, a blue lapis lazuli, and a white moonstone.
NLT.19: The third row will contain an orange jacinth, an agate, and a purple amethyst.
NLT.20: The fourth row will contain a blue-green beryl, an onyx, and a green jasper. All these stones will be set in gold filigree.
NLT.21: Each stone will represent one of the twelve sons of Israel, and the name of that tribe will be engraved on it like a seal.
NLT.22: “To attach the chestpiece to the ephod, make braided cords of pure gold thread.
NLT.23: Then make two gold rings and attach them to the top corners of the chestpiece.
NLT.24: Tie the two gold cords to the two rings on the chestpiece.
NLT.25: Tie the other ends of the cords to the gold settings on the shoulder-pieces of the ephod.
NLT.26: Then make two more gold rings and attach them to the inside edges of the chestpiece next to the ephod.
NLT.27: And make two more gold rings and attach them to the front of the ephod, below the shoulder-pieces, just above the knot where the decorative sash is fastened to the ephod.
NLT.28: Then attach the bottom rings of the chestpiece to the rings on the ephod with blue cords. This will hold the chestpiece securely to the ephod above the decorative sash.
NLT.29: “In this way, Aaron will carry the names of the tribes of Israel on the sacred chestpiece over his heart when he goes into the Holy Place. This will be a continual reminder that he represents the people when he comes before the LORD.
NLT.30: Insert the Urim and Thummim into the sacred chestpiece so they will be carried over Aaron’s heart when he goes into the LORD’s presence. In this way, Aaron will always carry over his heart the objects used to determine the LORD’s will for his people whenever he goes in before the LORD.
NLT.31: “Make the robe that is worn with the ephod from a single piece of blue cloth,
NLT.32: with an opening for Aaron’s head in the middle of it. Reinforce the opening with a woven collar so it will not tear.
NLT.33: Make pomegranates out of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and attach them to the hem of the robe, with gold bells between them.
NLT.34: The gold bells and pomegranates are to alternate all around the hem.
NLT.35: Aaron will wear this robe whenever he ministers before the LORD, and the bells will tinkle as he goes in and out of the LORD’s presence in the Holy Place. If he wears it, he will not die.
NLT.36: “Next make a medallion of pure gold, and engrave it like a seal with these words: HOLY TO THE LORD.
NLT.37: Attach the medallion with a blue cord to the front of Aaron’s turban, where it must remain.
NLT.38: Aaron must wear it on his forehead so he may take on himself any guilt of the people of Israel when they consecrate their sacred offerings. He must always wear it on his forehead so the LORD will accept the people.
NLT.39: “Weave Aaron’s patterned tunic from fine linen cloth. Fashion the turban from this linen as well. Also make a sash, and decorate it with colorful embroidery.
NLT.40: “For Aaron’s sons, make tunics, sashes, and special head coverings that are glorious and beautiful.
NLT.41: Clothe your brother, Aaron, and his sons with these garments, and then anoint and ordain them. Consecrate them so they can serve as my priests.
NLT.42: Also make linen undergarments for them, to be worn next to their bodies, reaching from their hips to their thighs.
NLT.43: These must be worn whenever Aaron and his sons enter the Tabernacle or approach the altar in the Holy Place to perform their priestly duties. Then they will not incur guilt and die. This is a permanent law for Aaron and all his descendants after him.

AMP.2: You are to make sacred garments [official clothing reserved for holy services] for Aaron your brother, for honor and for beauty (ornamentation).
AMP.3: Tell all the skilled and talented people whom I have endowed with a spirit of wisdom, that they are to make Aaron's garments to sanctify him and set him apart to serve as a priest for Me.
AMP.4: These are the garments which they shall make: a breastpiece and an ephod [for the breastpiece] and a robe and a tunic of checkered work, a turban, and a sash. They shall make sacred garments for Aaron your brother and his sons, so that he may serve as a priest to Me.
AMP.5: They are to use the gold and the blue and the purple and the scarlet fabric and fine twisted linen [from the people],
AMP.6: and they shall make the ephod of gold and blue, purple, and scarlet fabric and fine twisted linen, skillfully woven and [beautifully] worked.
AMP.7: It is to have two shoulder pieces joined to its two [back and front] ends, so that it may be joined together.
AMP.8: And the skillfully woven sash, which is on the ephod shall be made of the same material: of gold, of blue, purple, and scarlet fabric and fine twisted linen.
AMP.9: You shall take two onyx stones and engrave on them the names of the [twelve] sons of Israel,
AMP.10: six of their names on one stone and the remaining six names on the other stone, arranged in the order of their births.
AMP.11: With the work of a jeweler, like the engravings of a signet, you shall engrave the two stones according to the names of the sons of Israel. You shall have them set in filigree [settings] of gold.
AMP.12: You shall put the two stones on the [two] shoulder pieces of the ephod [of the high priest], as memorial stones for Israel; and Aaron shall bear their names on his two shoulders as a memorial before the LORD.
AMP.13: You shall make filigree [settings] of gold,
AMP.14: and you are to make two chains of pure gold like twisted cords, and fasten the corded chains to the settings.
AMP.15: "You are to make a breastpiece of judgment, the work of a skilled and talented craftsman; like the work of the ephod you shall make it: of gold, of blue, purple, and scarlet fabric and of fine twisted linen.
AMP.16: The breastpiece shall be square and folded double; a span [about nine inches] in length and a span in width.
AMP.17: You shall mount on it four rows of stones: the first row shall be a row of ruby, topaz, and emerald;
AMP.18: the second row a turquoise, a sapphire, and a diamond;
AMP.19: the third row a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst;
AMP.20: and the fourth row a beryl and an onyx and a jasper; they shall be set in gold filigree.
AMP.21: The [engraved] stones shall be twelve, according to the names of [the twelve tribes of] the sons of Israel; they shall be like the engravings of a signet, each with its name for the twelve tribes.
AMP.22: You shall make for the breastpiece chains of pure gold twisted like cords.
AMP.23: You shall make on the breastpiece two rings of gold, and shall put the two rings on the two ends of the breastpiece.
AMP.24: You shall put the two twisted cords of gold in the two rings which are on the ends of the breastpiece.
AMP.25: The other two ends of the two cords you shall fasten in the two filigree settings in front, putting them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod.
AMP.26: You shall make two gold rings and put them at the two ends of the breastpiece, on its inside edge next to the ephod.
AMP.27: You are to make two gold rings and attach them to the lower part of the two shoulder pieces of the ephod in front, close to the place where it is joined, above the skillfully woven sash of the ephod.
AMP.28: They shall bind the breastpiece by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a blue cord, so that it will be above the skillfully woven sash of the ephod, so that the breastpiece will not come loose from the ephod.
AMP.29: So Aaron shall carry the names of the sons of Israel (Jacob) in the breastpiece of judgment over his heart when he enters the Holy Place, to bring them in continual remembrance before the LORD.
AMP.30: In the breastpiece of judgment you shall put the Urim (Lights) and the Thummim (Perfections) [to be used for determining God's will in a matter]. They shall be over Aaron's heart whenever he goes before the LORD, and Aaron shall always carry the judgment (verdict, judicial decisions) of the sons of Israel over his heart before the LORD.
AMP.31: "And you shall make the robe of the ephod all of blue.
AMP.32: There shall be an opening at its top in the center [for the head], with a binding of woven work around the opening, like the opening in a coat of armor, so that it will not tear or fray.
AMP.33: You shall make pomegranates of blue, purple, and scarlet fabric all around its hem, with gold bells between them;
AMP.34: a golden bell and a pomegranate, a golden bell and a pomegranate, all around the [bottom] hem of the robe.
AMP.35: Aaron shall wear the robe when he ministers, and its sound shall be heard when he goes [alone] into the Holy Place before the LORD, and when he comes out, so that he will not die there.
AMP.36: "You shall also make a plate of pure gold and engrave on it, like the engravings of a signet, 'Holy to the LORD.'
AMP.37: You shall fasten it on the front of the turban with a blue cord.
AMP.38: It shall be on Aaron's forehead, and Aaron shall take away the guilt from the holy things which the sons of Israel dedicate, with regard to all their holy gifts. It shall always be on his forehead, so that they may be accepted before the LORD.
AMP.39: "You shall weave the tunic of checkered work of fine linen, and make a turban of fine linen. You shall make a sash, the work of an embroiderer.
AMP.40: "For Aaron's sons you shall make tunics and sashes and [ornamental] caps, for glory and honor and beauty.
AMP.41: You shall put the various articles of clothing on Aaron your brother and on his sons with him, and shall anoint them and ordain and sanctify them, so that they may serve Me as priests.
AMP.42: You shall make for them [white] linen undergarments to cover their bare flesh, reaching from the waist to the thighs.
AMP.43: The various articles of clothing shall be on Aaron and on his sons when they enter the Tent of Meeting, or when they approach the altar [of incense] to minister in the Holy Place, so that they do not incur guilt and die. It shall be a statute forever to Aaron and to his descendants after him.

NET.41: “You are to clothe them — your brother Aaron and his sons with him — and anoint them and ordain them and set them apart as holy, so that they may minister as my priests.
NET.42: Make for them linen undergarments to cover their naked bodies; they must cover from the waist to the thighs.
NET.43: These must be on Aaron and his sons when they enter to the tent of meeting, or when they approach the altar to minister in the Holy Place, so that they bear no iniquity and die. It is to be a perpetual ordinance for him and for his descendants after him.
